html:
On 2 July 1992 the Canadian government closed the northern cod fishery off Newfoundland, after the stock had collapsed to about one per cent of its former size. It was meant to last two years, but it never really ended for the old Dominion of Newfoundland, part of Canada since 1949.

Europeans had fished the Grand Banks since soon after Cabot's voyage of 1497. In the 1960s huge foreign factory trawlers took record catches, and after Canada claimed a 200 mile zone in 1977, its own fleet and poor science allowed overfishing to continue.

About 30,000 people lost their jobs in the largest layoff in Canadian history, and many outport villages emptied. The cod have only partly recovered. The collapse became a classic case of the tragedy of the commons, like the earlier fights of the Cod Wars.
